city_personality.one_line_summary: Beijing works best as a layered capital-city journey where imperial history, hutong texture, food memory, and modern contrast are arranged as executable routes instead of a generic checklist.
explore_strengths: heritage routes with strong historical weight
food rhythms that change by district and time of day
best_experience_modes: family-friendly landmark day with soft evening landing
signature_contrasts: imperial order versus everyday alley life
formal capital landmarks versus relaxed neighborhood wandering
traditional food memory versus modern urban dining
broad ceremonial scale versus intimate district texture
avoid_generic_framing: Do not reduce Beijing to only famous monuments.
Do not give every traveler type the same old-city opening and the same evening ending.
Do not use vague cultural praise without district texture.
Do not treat modern Beijing as interchangeable with any other big city.

district_knowledge.name: Imperial Core
district_knowledge.city_role: primary capital-history anchor and highest-recognition opening zone
mobility_notes: Use as one major anchor rather than stacking multiple heavy landmarks in the same day.
Morning-first routing is much stronger than late-day insertion.
Walking load compounds quickly if paired with too many large-format heritage stops.
route_use_cases: family iconic day when followed by softer district texture

district_knowledge.name: Hutong / Shichahai
district_knowledge.city_role: local-texture softener, citywalk core, and evening atmosphere zone
mobility_notes: Walking quality is high but total walking time can still be substantial.
Best used as a clustered half day rather than a quick stop between distant districts.
Evening value is much higher than forced midday pass-through.
route_use_cases: family soft landing after a heavier morning

district_knowledge.name: 798 Art District
district_knowledge.city_role: creative contemporary contrast anchor for premium non-generic Beijing routes
mobility_notes: Works best as an east-side dedicated half day.
Not a good filler between two old-city clusters.
Can become tiring if visitors try to over-cover galleries instead of choosing a clear route.
route_use_cases: solo slow-exploration creative district half day

district_knowledge.name: Sanlitun Modern Urban Core
district_knowledge.city_role: modern lifestyle, dining, and evening energy anchor
mobility_notes: Most effective as an evening closer rather than a full cultural day.
Weak if used as the only identity layer in a Beijing route.
Taxi and metro flexibility is important for late evening exits.
route_use_cases: solo modern-city contrast after old-city day

district_knowledge.name: Qianmen / Dashilar
district_knowledge.city_role: heritage-food and old-commercial-texture zone with strong route transition value
mobility_notes: Best when used as a food-and-texture extension after a nearby heritage anchor.
Main axis crowds can slow down family pacing during peak periods.
More rewarding in side lanes than in rushed pass-through mode.
route_use_cases: family and couple food-supported heritage day

district_knowledge.name: Temple of Heaven / South City
district_knowledge.city_role: open-space ceremonial heritage zone and southern food-culture bridge
signature_experiences: ceremonial architecture with more breathing room
mobility_notes: More open and manageable than some imperial-core routes, but still walking-heavy in hot weather.
Works well as a heritage day with food logic nearby, not as a late add-on after a large old-city morning.
Family pacing improves if the day includes rest and meal buffers.

district_knowledge.name: Olympic Park
district_knowledge.city_role: broad-space family-friendly and skyline-scale modern landmark zone
mobility_notes: Distance inside the park can be deceptively large.
Better for one focused open-space block than for chaining with dense old-city walking.
Night visual payoff is stronger than midday intensity.

district_knowledge.name: CBD / Guomao
district_knowledge.city_role: skyline, business-urban contrast, and polished modern Beijing layer
signature_experiences: elevated modern dining and night views
mobility_notes: Most useful as a contrast layer, not a whole-trip identity.
Can feel sterile if not paired with a stronger neighborhood or cultural zone elsewhere in the itinerary.
Works best from late afternoon onward when light and skyline atmosphere improve.
route_use_cases: solo reflective skyline walk after heritage-heavy days

poi_experience_knowledge.name: Forbidden City Main Visit
time_restriction_notes: Use early entry logic whenever possible.
Avoid making it the second heavy stop of the day.
Midday crowds sharply reduce relaxed-exploration value.
risks: Very high repetition risk across Beijing plans.
Can consume too much energy for family itineraries if the rest of the day remains heavy.
Weak as a default if the route needs more neighborhood texture than grand history.
poi_experience_knowledge.description: Use only when the plan truly needs Beijing's highest-recognition historical anchor.

poi_experience_knowledge.name: Jingshan Park Viewpoint
time_restriction_notes: Best when used after a heavy heritage block.
Late afternoon light often improves the photo payoff.
risks: Becomes formulaic if automatically paired with every old-city route.
Hill climb adds fatigue for young children after a long morning.
poi_experience_knowledge.description: A compact scenic release point that works well after history-heavy movement.

poi_experience_knowledge.name: Tiananmen Axis Exterior Walk
time_restriction_notes: Use as a short orientation layer rather than a full standalone block.
Peak-day security and crowd conditions can distort timing.
risks: Operational friction can outweigh experience value on crowded days.
Easy to overbuild symbolic weight with limited route payoff.
poi_experience_knowledge.description: Better as a framing move than as the emotional center of the whole day.

poi_experience_knowledge.name: Imperial Moat and Wall Edge Walk
time_restriction_notes: Best when the route needs calm after major landmark density.
risks: Can feel underpowered if used without a stronger nearby anchor.
poi_experience_knowledge.description: A useful quiet edge for routes that want to soften the imperial core.

poi_experience_knowledge.name: Shichahai Lakeside Walk
time_restriction_notes: Dusk and evening are materially stronger than flat midday visits.
Works well before or after a meal stop.
risks: Too generic if the route never leaves the main edge and fails to enter neighborhood texture.
Busy periods can reduce its relaxed quality.
poi_experience_knowledge.description: A signature atmosphere zone for routes that need warmth and walkable payoff.

poi_experience_knowledge.name: Bell and Drum Towers Edge Walk
time_restriction_notes: Best used as part of a flowing hutong route, not as an isolated stop.
risks: Can feel like a pass-through backdrop unless paired with side-lane exploration.
poi_experience_knowledge.description: Useful for shaping an old-city walk with recognizable historical texture.

poi_experience_knowledge.name: Nanluoguxiang Side Lanes
time_restriction_notes: Main lane alone is too generic; side-lane detours are the real value.
Better outside the heaviest crowd peaks.
risks: Very high overuse risk in youth-oriented Beijing plans.
Main-stream crowding can flatten local character.
poi_experience_knowledge.description: Use only when the route needs snack rhythm and younger lane energy, not as default hutong coverage.

poi_experience_knowledge.name: Yandai Xiejie Bend Walk
time_restriction_notes: Best as a short insert within a larger hutong route.
risks: Too small to carry a route by itself.
Can feel souvenir-heavy if not balanced with quieter nearby movement.
poi_experience_knowledge.description: A compact old-street detail layer rather than a main route anchor.

poi_experience_knowledge.name: 798 Core Gallery Lane Walk
time_restriction_notes: Best with a slower afternoon rhythm rather than a rushed cross-city insert.
risks: Can become visually repetitive if the route tries to over-cover the whole district.
Weak choice for family plans that need stronger ease and landmark clarity.
poi_experience_knowledge.description: A contemporary counterweight to old-city Beijing when the route needs creative energy.

poi_experience_knowledge.name: UCCA and Adjacent Gallery Cluster
time_restriction_notes: Works best when one or two focused gallery choices replace overcoverage.
risks: Less useful if the route already has too much formal culture and not enough movement variety.
poi_experience_knowledge.description: A stronger premium insert than a broad undirected sweep of the whole district.

poi_experience_knowledge.name: 751 D-Park Industrial Spine
time_restriction_notes: Best used when the route wants industrial visual contrast, not just gallery hopping.
risks: Can feel empty if there is no adjacent food or cafe logic.
poi_experience_knowledge.description: Useful when a 798 route needs spatial variation and less gallery-only pacing.

poi_experience_knowledge.name: 798 Courtyard Cafe Loop
time_restriction_notes: Most useful as a tempo-control tool inside a longer creative district half day.
risks: Can become filler if the overall route lacks a stronger cultural or visual anchor.
poi_experience_knowledge.description: A useful pacing device for premium slower routes.

poi_experience_knowledge.name: Taikoo Li Urban Walk
time_restriction_notes: Stronger in late afternoon and evening than daytime.
Best after a route that already established Beijing-specific texture elsewhere.
risks: Can feel globally generic if the day lacks local context.
Weak primary choice for family sample routes.
poi_experience_knowledge.description: Use as a contrastive modern-energy finish, not as the entire identity of Beijing.

poi_experience_knowledge.name: Workers Stadium Perimeter Walk
time_restriction_notes: Best used as an atmosphere transition around dinner or nightlife movement.
risks: Can feel thin if not embedded within a larger Sanlitun urban route.
poi_experience_knowledge.description: A short city-energy insert rather than a destination by itself.

poi_experience_knowledge.name: Embassy Area Cafe Streets
time_restriction_notes: Useful before the district becomes fully night-oriented.
risks: Lacks strong Beijing specificity if used without contrastive old-city content in the itinerary.
poi_experience_knowledge.description: Useful for premium slower routes that need a quieter modern-city layer.

poi_experience_knowledge.name: Sanlitun Night Spine
time_restriction_notes: Night value only; weak daytime route contribution.
risks: Too generic if used without a clear traveler-type reason.
Not appropriate as a standard family route layer.
poi_experience_knowledge.description: Use sparingly and intentionally for urban-night energy.

poi_experience_knowledge.name: Qianmen Pedestrian Axis
time_restriction_notes: Best when followed by side-lane texture or food logic, not as a pure crowd corridor.
risks: Crowding can quickly reduce route quality.
Main-axis-only use feels generic.
poi_experience_knowledge.description: Use as a bridge between big heritage and edible old-city texture.

poi_experience_knowledge.name: Dashilar Side Lanes
time_restriction_notes: Stronger when the route slows down and enters smaller lanes instead of staying on the main strip.
risks: Can blur into generic old-street tourism if the route lacks focus.
Weak for very compressed family schedules.
poi_experience_knowledge.description: A more useful premium zone than the main corridor when the route needs old-city texture.

poi_experience_knowledge.name: Yangmeizhu Xiejie
time_restriction_notes: Useful when the route wants a smaller, calmer old-street detail.
risks: Too subtle to carry a route alone.
Needs stronger anchor nearby.
poi_experience_knowledge.description: A fine-grained premium insert for routes avoiding the most obvious old-city flow.

poi_experience_knowledge.name: Zhengyangmen and Arrow Tower Exterior
time_restriction_notes: Best as a visual framing move at route start or transition.
risks: Low standalone payoff if treated as a full attraction stop.
poi_experience_knowledge.description: A framing landmark that works best as part of a stronger food-texture route.

poi_experience_knowledge.name: Temple of Heaven Main Visit
time_restriction_notes: Morning or late morning is stronger than late-day fatigue use.
Works best with a lighter second half nearby.
risks: Can feel redundant if paired with another monumental heritage anchor the same day.
Open exposure becomes tiring in summer heat.
poi_experience_knowledge.description: A more breathable ceremonial landmark than the imperial core, but still a real time-and-energy block.

poi_experience_knowledge.name: Tiantan Cypress Loop
time_restriction_notes: Useful after the main ceremonial stop when the route needs breathing room.
risks: Low payoff if the day already lacks a stronger anchor.
poi_experience_knowledge.description: A practical pacing tool for routes that need calm without leaving the area.

poi_experience_knowledge.name: South City Breakfast Street Walk
time_restriction_notes: Morning-only value; weak later in the day.
risks: Needs nearby route logic or it becomes just a meal stop.
poi_experience_knowledge.description: A non-monument opening for routes that want more lived-in south-city rhythm.

poi_experience_knowledge.name: Hongqiao and South-City Edge Glimpse
time_restriction_notes: Works only as a short route texture layer.
risks: Too practical to anchor a premium route alone.
poi_experience_knowledge.description: A small contrast note for routes that want less postcard and more city edge.

poi_experience_knowledge.name: Olympic Green Central Axis
time_restriction_notes: Late afternoon and evening are significantly stronger than midday.
risks: Feels too spatially empty if the whole day lacks a stronger cultural or neighborhood layer.
poi_experience_knowledge.description: Useful as a spacious reset or family-friendly skyline day component.

poi_experience_knowledge.name: Bird's Nest Exterior View
time_restriction_notes: Night lighting improves payoff considerably.
risks: Low standalone value if treated as a deep cultural stop.
poi_experience_knowledge.description: A strong visual marker, best used within a broader open-space or skyline route.

poi_experience_knowledge.name: Water Cube Night Exterior
time_restriction_notes: Night-value only; daytime use is weak.
risks: Not enough by itself to justify a long cross-city move.
poi_experience_knowledge.description: A short high-payoff night visual insert.

poi_experience_knowledge.name: Olympic Forest South Loop
time_restriction_notes: Stronger in mild weather and later afternoon light.
risks: Too low-intensity for routes that still need strong city identity that day.
poi_experience_knowledge.description: Useful when a premium family sample needs one non-exhausting day.

poi_experience_knowledge.name: CCTV Headquarters Exterior Walk
time_restriction_notes: Best when used within a skyline or modern-business district walk.
risks: Can feel cold and abstract if the itinerary lacks more human-scale texture elsewhere.
poi_experience_knowledge.description: Useful for showcasing Beijing's business-core architecture without letting it dominate the trip.

poi_experience_knowledge.name: China World Terrace and Mall Edge Walk
time_restriction_notes: Late afternoon to evening gives the strongest city-light contrast.
risks: Can slide into generic mall tourism if not tied to skyline or route contrast logic.
poi_experience_knowledge.description: A polished modern finish for routes that need controlled skyline atmosphere.

poi_experience_knowledge.name: Guomao Skyline Canyon Walk
time_restriction_notes: Much stronger at dusk and night than in flat midday light.
risks: Not enough local warmth for a route that lacks older-city or neighborhood material elsewhere.
poi_experience_knowledge.description: A clear skyline contrast move for premium urban-night routes.

poi_experience_knowledge.name: Tonghui River Edge Urban Walk
time_restriction_notes: Best for quieter late-day modern routes.
risks: Too subtle to justify a special trip without nearby stronger anchors.
poi_experience_knowledge.description: A calmer modern edge useful for solo and couple routes that want less retail-heavy CBD pacing.

food_knowledge.name: Qianmen Traditional Snack and Dessert Run
food_knowledge.note: Best when used to support an old-city route rather than as a stand-alone food day.

food_knowledge.name: Dashilar Side-Lane Bakery and Cafe Mix
food_knowledge.note: Useful when the route wants a more editorial old-city texture than a pure snack corridor.

food_knowledge.name: Shichahai Hutong Dinner Rhythm
food_knowledge.note: Best when the route already earned enough time to enjoy the district rather than rushing through.

food_knowledge.name: Nanluo Snack-Grazing Logic
food_knowledge.note: Useful only when the route wants flexibility and youth energy, not as the default food logic for every hutong day.

food_knowledge.name: South-City Breakfast and Lunch Corridor
food_knowledge.note: Best for routes that want daily-life food rhythm instead of polished dining.

food_knowledge.name: South-City Copper-Pot and Warm Meal Logic
food_knowledge.note: Especially useful in cooler seasons when the route needs comfort and recovery.

food_knowledge.name: 798 Cafe and Brunch Pattern
food_knowledge.note: Works best when used to control pace inside a curated 798 half day.

food_knowledge.name: Sanlitun Modern Dining Close
food_knowledge.note: Best as a modern contrast finish after a route that already established more local Beijing identity.

food_knowledge.name: Guomao Polished Business Lunch Layer
food_knowledge.note: Should be used sparingly so the route does not lose Beijing-specific food identity.

food_knowledge.name: Olympic Park Casual Family Meal Logic
food_knowledge.note: Not a destination food layer, but useful for keeping family sample routes executable.

preferred_route_patterns: one heavy anchor plus one soft district
open-space recovery day after a monument-heavy day
meal-supported pacing with low surprise friction
heritage morning plus scenic or hutong dusk
creative afternoon plus polished dinner close
slower final day with texture rather than checklist pressure
avoid_patterns: nightlife with no emotional route build-up

preferred_route_patterns: one iconic layer plus neighborhood or snack texture
low-cost wandering with a clear route center
avoid_patterns: landmark-only days with little local playfulness

preferred_route_patterns: one anchor plus flexible wandering district
heritage and skyline contrast across different days
slower routes with room for pause
avoid_patterns: couple-coded date-night logic as the main value
high-friction transfer chains with weak payoff

peak_season_notes: Major old-city landmarks can dominate the entire day during holidays if entry timing is not managed early.
Qianmen and other high-recognition corridors lose some premium quality when crowd density turns the route into slow procession.
When holiday crowd pressure is high, district clustering matters more than route ambition.
queue_behavior_notes: Forbidden City type anchors should not be paired casually with multiple other queue-prone heritage stops.
High-queue landmarks should usually be the first major commitment of the day, not a midday add-on.
If queues consume the emotional center of the day, the route needs a softer second half nearby rather than another hard ticketed block.
walking_load_notes: Imperial-core routes often look compact on paper but become physically heavy in practice.
Hutong and Shichahai routes feel relaxed yet still involve meaningful walking time.
Summer heat sharply increases fatigue cost for exposed heritage and open-space days.
time_limit_notes: Some night-value zones such as Sanlitun and Water Cube are not meaningful daytime anchors.
Breakfast-style south-city routes lose their identity after the morning window.
798 is stronger as a dedicated slower half day than as a rushed route fragment.
booking_notes: High-recognition monuments should be treated as booking-sensitive and timing-sensitive in premium sample planning.
Premium routes should avoid assuming spontaneous access to every top landmark in peak periods.
family_friction_notes: Family premium routes should avoid more than one high-walking anchor in a single day.
Open-space recovery days are valuable and should not be treated as weak content days.
Meal access and rest rhythm are part of route quality, not secondary details.
night_mobility_notes: Night-value districts work best when the route closes nearby instead of forcing a long final transfer.
Modern evening districts should be used intentionally for couple/student/solo routes, not copied across all templates.

half_day_combinations.name: Imperial Morning Plus Soft Old-City Finish
half_day_combinations.logic: Use one heavy capital-history anchor first, then move into more walkable texture and food support.

half_day_combinations.name: Temple of Heaven Plus South-City Food Rhythm
half_day_combinations.logic: Use a more breathable ceremonial landmark followed by south-central food and heritage-commercial texture.

half_day_combinations.name: 798 Creative Afternoon Plus Sanlitun Evening
half_day_combinations.logic: Contemporary visual culture first, urban dinner and evening energy second.

half_day_combinations.name: Olympic Broad-Space Relief Block
half_day_combinations.logic: Use when the itinerary needs spacious movement and lower cultural density.

one_day_route_shapes.name: Classic Beijing Premium Shape
one_day_route_shapes.start_logic: Begin with one iconic anchor early.
one_day_route_shapes.midday_rhythm: Shift into food or viewpoint support rather than stacking another heavy ticketed stop.
one_day_route_shapes.afternoon_transition: Move into hutong or side-lane texture.
one_day_route_shapes.evening_close: Use lakeside or casual old-city dinner rather than forcing a distant modern zone.

one_day_route_shapes.name: East-Side Creative Contrast Shape
one_day_route_shapes.start_logic: Keep the day east-side from the beginning.
one_day_route_shapes.midday_rhythm: Use 798 or another creative core as the main slow block.
one_day_route_shapes.afternoon_transition: Reduce transfer count and allow cafe or gallery pacing.
one_day_route_shapes.evening_close: Finish in Sanlitun or CBD depending on traveler type.

one_day_route_shapes.name: Family Soft Heritage Shape
one_day_route_shapes.start_logic: Use one clear landmark with easy orientation.
one_day_route_shapes.midday_rhythm: Insert meal and rest support early enough.
one_day_route_shapes.afternoon_transition: Move into open, lower-pressure walking or park-like texture.
one_day_route_shapes.evening_close: Close close to the day zone without nightlife pressure.

multi_day_balance_rules: Do not place the two most physically expensive heritage days back-to-back in family 5-day templates.
For 3-day routes, do not let all three days open with the same monument-heavy pattern.
At least one day in student and solo templates should be neighborhood- or creative-district-led rather than landmark-led.
Modern districts should appear as contrast layers, not replace Beijing-specific city identity.

avoid_combinations.reason: Too transfer-heavy and too thematically fragmented for a premium one-day route.
Can become an over-monument day unless the rest of the route is dramatically softened.
Creates an awkward long-distance contrast day with weak route flow for most sample plans.

backup_logic: If a heavy iconic landmark becomes operationally too risky, switch to a neighborhood-led day in Hutong / Shichahai or Qianmen / Dashilar rather than forcing another big-ticket substitute.
If weather or fatigue weakens a planned long walk, shorten the district count and protect the food-and-evening logic instead of preserving every stop.
diversification_rules: Do not use Forbidden City as the mandatory first-day anchor for every Beijing sample.
Rotate between old-city heritage-led, hutong-led, south-city-led, and east-side modern-contrast route centers.
Use food logic as a differentiator rather than repeating one generic Beijing dinner pattern.

route_templates.design_goal: Affordable, youthful, flexible, and clearly different from family or couple logic.

day_templates.theme: Iconic but not over-formal old-city entry
day_templates.route_shape: One lighter iconic anchor plus food-backed heritage-commercial texture.
must_have_traits: Use snack or low-cost meal rhythm.
Keep enough freedom for casual wandering.

day_templates.route_shape: Slow afternoon creative district plus lively modern evening.
must_have_traits: Let modern Beijing feel youthful, not premium-only.

day_templates.route_shape: Flexible wandering day with food grazing and optional scenic close.
must_have_traits: Visible contrast from day 1 and day 2.

route_templates.design_goal: Atmospheric, photogenic, and emotionally paced rather than monument-stacked.

day_templates.theme: Heritage scale plus romantic old-city atmosphere
day_templates.route_shape: History anchor, scenic release, then hutong / lakeside evening.

day_templates.theme: Creative contrast and polished dinner close
day_templates.route_shape: Slower visual afternoon and a stylish urban night finish.
must_have_traits: The route should feel like a mood arc.

day_templates.route_shape: Less checklist pressure, more shared wandering and food memory.

route_templates.design_goal: Clear, iconic, low-friction, and genuinely executable over multiple days.

day_templates.route_shape: Recognizable old-city entry with meal access and manageable walking.
must_have_traits: Do not burn too much energy on arrival day.

day_templates.route_shape: One major heritage anchor and one softer nearby afternoon/evening landing.
Open-space heritage with gentler pacing and south-city meal support.
must_have_traits: This day should feel easier than day 2.

day_templates.theme: Open-space recovery and modern skyline relief
day_templates.route_shape: Broad-space family-friendly route with lower cultural density.
must_have_traits: Use recovery as a quality feature, not dead time.

day_templates.route_shape: Shorter walkable texture and flexible meal close.
must_have_traits: Keep packing and departure realities in mind.

route_templates.design_goal: Self-directed, layered, and rich in observation value without feeling empty or generic.

day_templates.theme: Capital-history anchor plus reflective old-city walking
day_templates.route_shape: One clear anchor followed by a more open-ended neighborhood walk.
must_have_traits: Do not overschedule the second half.

day_templates.route_shape: From contemporary creative texture into quieter skyline contrast.
must_have_traits: Independent pace matters more than volume.

day_templates.route_shape: Local rhythm, morning food logic, and reflective close instead of climax-chasing.

all_year_notes: District clustering is more important than total POI count in Beijing because movement cost rises quickly once the route spans too many zones.
Old-city and modern-east-side content should usually live on different route shapes unless the itinerary is explicitly contrast-driven.
seasonal_highlights: Spring and autumn strengthen citywalk-heavy districts such as Hutong / Shichahai and Dashilar side lanes.
Cooler months make shared warming meal logic in south-city routes more valuable.
weather_sensitive_notes: Summer heat punishes exposed monument and broad-axis days.
Winter wind lowers the value of long open-space walking unless the day is built around short high-payoff exterior moments.
day_vs_night_notes: Hutong / Shichahai and Olympic lighting routes improve at dusk and night.
Sanlitun and CBD are much stronger late than early.
weekday_vs_weekend_notes: High-traffic old-city corridors degrade more on weekends and holidays.
Modern districts tolerate crowding better than heritage corridors when used as evening closers.

editor_notes: This file is intentionally selective rather than exhaustive.
The focus is premium route quality, traveler differentiation, and execution feasibility.
POI list is curated to support the first batch of high-quality Explore samples.
